videos.script: Look at the three routers in the lab side by side. Their configurations are almost the same. A hostname, two interfaces, a loopback, OSPF, and a few lines that never change. {{same}} What really differs between them is about ten values. {{values}} So write the repeated text once, as a template with holes in it. Put each router's values in a small file of its own. Rendering fills the holes, one configuration per router. {{render}} In this lesson you build that template for the lab, in Jinja2. You make it refuse a missing value instead of printing nothing. And you check that it reproduces the three routers exactly, down to the last byte. {{check}} Then a change starts in the data, and only the router that changed receives anything. And a line somebody typed by hand is no longer the truth. {{push}}
